Fix flaky reconnect in the event stream
The event stream drops after the laptop sleeps, and the sidebar stops updating until I reload. Can you find out why and fix it?
I'll start with how the client opens the stream and what it does when it goes quiet.

The server sends a heartbeat every 10 seconds, but  stream.ts  only reconnects on an  error  event. When the machine sleeps, the TCP connection goes half-open: the browser never sees an error, so the client waits forever.
Two smaller problems make it worse:
backoff.ts  resets its delay on every message, so a flapping server is retried at full speed.
The sidebar store ignores  session.updated  events that arrive before the first list fetch.
Treat silence as failure. If no event or heartbeat arrives for 25 seconds, close the stream and reconnect with backoff:
I also moved the backoff reset to after a stream has stayed healthy for a minute.
Done. The stream now recovers from sleep on its own.
Watchdog:  stream.ts  closes and reopens the stream after 25 s of silence.
Backoff: the delay only resets after a minute of healthy traffic.
Sidebar: early  session.updated  events are queued until the list loads.

The reviewer agreed and suggested one change, which I applied: the watchdog now also restarts on  visibilitychange , so waking the laptop reconnects immediately instead of after 25 s. All 14 tests in  src/net  pass.
Nice. Can you add a test for the backoff, so the reset can't regress?
I'll add a test that drives the backoff with a fake clock, so it can check both the growth and the reset rule.
a flapping server that fails right after each message, which must keep backing off;
a stream that stays healthy for a minute, which resets the delay;
the cap, so retries never wait longer than 30 seconds.

With the old reset-on-every-message rule this test fails on the second delay, which is exactly the regression you were worried about. The healthy-minute case uses the same clock and advances it by 61 seconds before the next failure.
